issues.failure_explanation: The three bounds are stated as exact inequalities with no multiplicative constant, and (i) sums over $s\ge n/\log n$ although the approximation space has dimension $m=\lfloor n/(20\log n)\rfloor$. The proof only invokes the cited least squares results (KU21, BSU23, DKU2023), which hold with unspecified absolute constants and with the sum starting at the dimension $m$ of the approximation space (or its cited analogue). Since the error of the least squares projection onto $V_m$ is at least $d_m\ge$ the tail starting at $n/\log n$ for suitable spectra, and the cited theorems carry constants, the constant-free statements are not supported as written (also (iii) refers to $S_{c_2n}^X$ instead of $S_{c_3n}^X$).

issues.failure_explanation: $S_{c_3n}^X$ uses $c_3n>n$ sample points, so by definition of the sampling width it only bounds $\varrho_{c_3n}$, not $\varrho_n$. The first inequality in (iii) (and its copy in theorem:varrho_n><(iii) and in the Introduction) would require $\varrho_n\ll\varrho_{c_3 n}$ uniformly, which is not established and is not true in general for a fixed $\bsigma$ with rapidly decaying $\sigma_s^{-1}$: $\varrho_n$ can be of order $d_{n/c}$ while the $c_3n$-point least squares error is of order $d_n$. The proof gives no argument for this step.
